pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: src/features/agents/quick-answer/triage/triageAdapters.ts:590 the deck classifies a review whose severity is missing as medium (an unrecognised token falls to weight 50 at :667) with no marker, so on the surface where the verdict is given an unreadable payload is spelled as a readable medium and sorted under real highs - while the manual-review list resolves the same row to Unclassified with a defaulted marker (src/features/overview/sub_manual-review/libs/reviewHelpers.ts:37)

techniques.evidence: src/features/agents/quick-answer/triage/triageAdapters.ts:590 `review.severity || 'medium'` - quiet mild default with no defaulted marker; the loud resolveReviewSeverity exists but this adapter does not use it

src/features/agents/quick-answer/triage/useUnifiedTriage.ts:1075 optimistic removal is restored when the write throws (realized), and idea/policy/evolution verdicts carry a seen-status CAS (src/features/agents/quick-answer/triage/triageDispatch.ts:52); but goals have no compare-and-swap (triageDispatch.ts:81), so two reviewers can both decide the same goal, and the deck kinds (src/features/agents/quick-answer/triage/triageTypes.ts:28) omit companion approvals and held trigger fires, so the unified queue is not complete by construction
src/features/agents/quick-answer/triage/triageDispatch.ts:12 every verdict defers, writes or throws - no branch resolves a card without a write; reviews land through a pending-only CAS in the backend

pairs.registryProposal: one review-severity vocabulary now has three classifiers in this repo (a loud one in reviewHelpers.ts, an Info fall-through in reviewFocusHelpers.tsx, a medium fall-through here); fail-loud-classification-default could name 'a loud resolver exists but a second consumer re-implements the fall-through' as its commonest field failure and point at one-validation-door for the fix

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/dispatch.rs:1235 any persona run can resolve any OPEN incident by id prefix - including a persona_blocker escalation another persona raised for a human - and that resolve (:1256) is what makes incident_continuation re-run the blocked work (src-tauri/src/engine/incident_continuation.rs:7); the resolved row records no decider (src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/audit_incidents.rs:484), so a machine answer to a human-addressed handoff is indistinguishable from a human one except in free-text notes

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/dispatch.rs:1235 the answerer of a persona_blocker escalation is not resolved at raise time; any execution emitting resolve_incident with a matching prefix answers it
src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/audit_incidents.rs:484 resolve writes status, resolved_at and a free-text note only; there is no resolved_by, and acknowledged_by is hardcoded to user (:464)
src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/audit_incidents.rs:439 apply_transition reads the status, validates the move, then UPDATEs WHERE id = ? only (:485) - a read-then-write two deciders can both win
src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/audit_incidents.rs:579 the continuation is claimed with continued_at IS NULL before any work, so a resolved blocker re-runs at most once
src/features/overview/sub_incidents/libs/incidentTaxonomy.ts:86 an unreadable severity ranks above critical, and isUnclassifiedSeverity (:69) is the machine-readable marker

pairs.registryProposal: the map paired this UI context on severity/escalate tokens, but the governing flow (persona raise_incident -> resolve -> auto-continuation) lives in engine files outside the context; the subject applies, through a door the matcher could not see

pairs.evidence: src/features/onboarding/components/useOnboardingState.ts:164 one Approve click grants the connector manifest capabilities fetched AFTER the click, so the user never saw what they consented to (the card shows only a SAFE/REVIEW badge from a hand-kept list, src/features/onboarding/components/DesktopDiscoveryStep.tsx:47); and when no manifest comes back, :166 still marks the app Approved with nothing written

techniques.evidence: src/features/onboarding/components/useOnboardingState.ts:164 the disclosure does not derive from the bound action: capabilities (desktop_terminal = ProcessSpawn+FileWrite) are granted unseen, and the risk badge is an enumerated set (DesktopDiscoveryStep.tsx:47), not the capability set
src/features/onboarding/components/useOnboardingState.ts:166 a null manifest skips the grant write yet the surface shows Approved - a decision that did not land, spelled as one

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: src/lib/harness/executor.ts:49 the area write scope is a prompt line the executor may waive ('unless absolutely necessary'), the session runs at the project root (:167) with Edit/Write/Bash and skipPermissions true (src/lib/harness/run-harness.ts:165), and nothing compares the diff to area.scope or records a widening - the trust boundary lives inside the context the executor can override

techniques.evidence: src/lib/harness/executor.ts:49 the fixed tier (allowed paths) is carried as waivable prose, with no enforcement and no amendment record of an out-of-scope write
src/lib/harness/run-harness.ts:156 an operator-launched autonomous loop with no human gate in it; the subject reaches it only through its scope-of-work flow
